parts.name: Agent plugins
parts.caption: Which hooks each agent runs
parts.purpose: Small config folders, one per agent, that decide which of its events reach the hook and name the agent to it.

holds.name: Claude Code's plugin
holds.text: The hooks Claude Code runs on each event, installed with `claude plugin`.

holds.name: The other agents' configs
holds.text: agy's, Copilot's and Qwen Code's plugin or extension, and Codex's and Cursor's user-level hook files.

holds.name: Rendering
holds.text: `plotkeeper install` fills each with the path of the hook binaries in the data folder's `bin/` before it installs it.

parts.name: Hook
parts.caption: Records every agent event
parts.purpose: Runs on each agent event and appends it to the event log. It also holds a question, a plan or a permission open until you answer.

holds.name: The event log
holds.text: One append-only JSON Lines file, the only source of session state.

holds.name: The recorder
holds.text: Appends each event with the agent its entry names, and drops another harness's event, which that harness records.

holds.name: IDE sessions
holds.text: Records no process for an agent inside an IDE app such as VS Code, so its session goes idle instead of ending.

holds.name: The answer hook
holds.text: Waits for your answer to a question, a plan or a permission, given on the page; a command auto mode blocked goes on to your agent at once.

holds.name: The process check
holds.text: The one test of whether a pid is alive, which the answer hook and the server both use.

parts.name: Core
parts.caption: Turns events into session state
parts.purpose: Plain Rust logic that reads the event log's lines in order and knows every session's turns, checks, subagents and whether it needs you.

holds.name: The agent adapters
holds.text: Turn each agent's hook line into one neutral event: Claude Code, agy, Codex, Copilot, Cursor and Qwen Code.

holds.name: Session state
holds.text: The sessions, their turns and subagents, and whether one needs you, from the events one at a time.

holds.name: The step ledger
holds.text: One row for every tool call of a session, its workers' included, and which of them were checks.

holds.name: The transcript reader
holds.text: A tolerant reader of a session's transcript, for what the session is doing and why.

parts.name: Server
parts.caption: Holds the state, answers the commands
parts.purpose: The `plotkeeper` program: it holds the state, follows the event log and serves the page on 127.0.0.1, with one function for each of the page's commands.

holds.name: Serving the page
holds.text: The built page, a POST route per command and one event stream, which also carries logged errors, behind a token, a cookie and a Host check.

holds.name: The read loop
holds.text: Follows the event log and sends what changed (the list, the selection, the brief, notices, the text of the settings files) to the page.

holds.name: Settings and projects
holds.text: The writer, its API keys in plotkeeper's own Keychain entries, the settings and the saved project list.

holds.name: The programs
holds.text: `plotkeeper`, which starts the server and opens the page, and `plotkeeper-run`, the launcher of one background run.

parts.name: Install
parts.caption: Wires the agents to the hook
parts.purpose: `plotkeeper install` and `uninstall`: copies the hook into the data folder and wires each agent it finds to that copy, through the agent's own command where it has one.

holds.name: Agent wiring
holds.text: Renders each agent's plugin or hook file with the hook's path and installs it, and takes that back on uninstall.

holds.name: Hook copies
holds.text: The hook binaries copied into the data folder's `bin/`, so an agent runs a copy that a rebuild does not move.

parts.name: Map engine
parts.caption: Reads code into parts and links
parts.purpose: The `system-map` crate and command: checks a repository's `system-map.json` against its files, says which part owns each path, proves its links with the language extractors and counts how parts follow imports.

holds.name: Ownership
holds.text: Which part owns each tracked file, by the last pattern that matches, and which parts a list of paths touches.

holds.name: Part text
holds.text: A part's purpose and held items with their caps, and the conversion of a version 1 map.

holds.name: Extractors and links
holds.text: One module per language behind one contract, turning files into edges that prove or fail each import link.

holds.name: Imports
holds.text: `system-map imports`: how well the parts follow the code's imports, counted per importing file.

holds.name: Laws
holds.text: Finds the `@law:` tags that tie tests to laws.

holds.name: Commit mode
holds.text: Reads a commit's files and their text without checking it out, for `--commit`.

parts.name: Map, briefs and runs
parts.caption: Map data, briefs, agent runs
parts.purpose: What the Map view and the briefs show, and the runs started from them: the map with its fog, history and ratify, PR briefs and catch-ups, and the headless agent runs.

holds.name: The map
holds.text: Reads the map from the default branch, with its fog, history, staleness, CI laws, what you ratified and a PR's Map diff.

holds.name: Briefs
holds.text: PR lookups, the PR briefs of ready PRs, part catch-ups, the pre-flight and the end-of-story bar.

holds.name: Background runs
holds.text: Sandboxed runs on your click, one per project; the map text review starts itself on your PRs and reads a PR's head, its prompt no PR text.

holds.name: The quiet log
holds.text: One line per thing you use, kept for the stop rules, with nothing shown.

parts.name: Understanding
parts.caption: Writes what you read, and keeps it
parts.purpose: Decides what a change is worth telling you, asks the writer for it and stores what comes back.

holds.name: The writer contract
holds.text: One call shape for every writer, run as a program or, for an API-key writer, over HTTP.

holds.name: Turn writing
holds.text: What a turn's end writes: its summary and its session's brief, held to the facts.

holds.name: PR briefs and part catch-ups
holds.text: Facts code assembles, the writer's story of them and the code checks on its reply.

holds.name: Pre-flight
holds.text: The parts of the map a piece of work will likely cross, predicted before it starts.

holds.name: The store
holds.text: The briefs, summaries and the decision history's risk notes on disk; cards are retired, and those stored before stay readable.

parts.name: Window
parts.caption: Everything you see and press
parts.purpose: The page: the Map view as its base, beside the session list. It shows state and sends your actions to the server.

holds.name: The Map view
holds.text: The parts, links and fog, a part's sheet with history and ratify, the PR brief, panels' explanations, pre-flight and micro-world overlays.

holds.name: The session list
holds.text: A header for every saved project, even one with no sessions, whose headers switch the map.

holds.name: The left panel
holds.text: A session's story, History, a turn's diff, a worker's log or Settings, open over the map.

holds.name: The writer's settings
holds.text: Pick the program that writes the summaries, or set up an API-key writer, and test it with one tiny call.

holds.name: Patch review
holds.text: A back a law run's proven test patch, to open as a draft PR or discard.

holds.name: Wait tips
holds.text: While a session runs, one line in its Intention box teaches one feature, chosen with a cooldown; settings can turn them off.

holds.name: What's new
holds.text: After an update to a new version, one toast with a link to that version's GitHub Release.

holds.name: Hints
holds.text: `hint()` gives a control or a mark its own hover; the snap hover rule fails a control without one and any `title`.

parts.name: Workbench
parts.caption: Worktrees and PRs
parts.purpose: The one runner of `git` and `gh`, git worktrees and fetches, other agents' resume commands, and agy's plugin. A black box: it never fogs.

holds.name: The runner
holds.text: Builds every `git` and `gh` with prompts off and no input, and runs commands to a deadline that kills their process group.

holds.name: Git
holds.text: A folder's main checkout, `origin`'s fetch and what removing a worktree would lose, never with force.

links.reason: Each agent reads its plugin's hook config to learn which events to send to the hook.
Each plugin's hooks run the hook binaries on an agent event, with the event on standard input.
Install embeds the plugins' hook files at build time and writes each agent's copy with the hook's path filled in.
The hook appends each event to the event log, which the server follows.
Understanding runs the writer's program for each summary or brief; an API-key writer is asked over HTTP instead.
The server serves the page, a route per command and one event stream over HTTP on 127.0.0.1.
Workbench runs git to fetch from origin and `gh` to look up PRs.
Workbench embeds agy's plugin files at build time and installs them.
The runner starts headless agent runs, such as back a law and micro-worlds, in a sandbox.
Install runs each agent's own install command, such as `claude plugin` or `qwen extensions`.
Workbench runs the `agy` command to install and remove agy's plugin.

laws.text: Every `git` and `gh` the workspace starts is built by the runner, so none can wait on a prompt.
Install and uninstall reach Claude Code only through `claude plugin` and never open its settings file.
Install and uninstall reach Qwen Code only through `qwen extensions` and never open its settings file, which can hold API keys.
The hook never makes the agent wait, except for your answer.
A saved project stays after its sessions end or are deleted, and leaves only through Remove project.
The core does no I/O except reading transcripts.
A check's result is its last run's.
The window's types and the Rust types of the server's replies agree, and each command's argument names are its handler's; a reply built as bare JSON has none.
A session's pieces are written one at a time, in order.
A stored file of an older format still loads.
Replaying the log never rewrites, replaces or deletes a stored card, summary or answer.

A change is untrusted text: the writer has no tools where it can turn them off (Claude; Copilot's allow-list naming no tool, with its built-in MCP servers off, checked in wave 1's trial), else it runs read-only (Codex's read-only sandbox, Cursor's ask mode) or as locked as its flags allow (agy's sandboxed terminal, with no slash commands or skills), always in an empty folder.
Loud colour is only for what needs you and for a broken law.

hops.text: Core sees the turn end and the server asks for its summary; this hop runs from core to the server, against the import link.
The server passes the request on; understanding queues it for the session.
Understanding asks the writer for the summary, and for the session's Goal and Design so far.
The writer's reply comes back and understanding stores it.
Understanding tells the server the brief changed; this hop runs back against the import link.
